none: This segment contains only Qur'an text, without commentary.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses al-rufāt as dust; another definition is matter pulverized into fragments, with the verb meaning to break into pieces.
rows.anchor: الرفات قال الفراء: التراب. وقيل: الذي بولغ في دقه حتى تفتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form rifāt denotes broken, fragmented pieces, like ḥuṭām, futāt, riḍāḍ, and duqāq.
rows.anchor: والرفات الأجزاء المتفتتة من كل شيء مكسر، وفعال بناء لهذا المعنى كالحطام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical reading is the past-tense verb qaḍā, widely transmitted among the seven readers and also reported from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور وقضى فعلا ماضيا من القضاء.

rows.speaker: بعض ولد معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: A variant reads qaḍāʾu as an initial nominative verbal noun, with an taʿbudū as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعض ولد معاذ بن جبل:

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأصحابه وابن عباس وابن جبير والنخعي وميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Their codex reading uses wording from the root of waṣiyya; another group read awṣā, which Abū Ḥayyān treats as explanatory rather than a canonical reading.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود وأصحابه وابن عباس وابن جبير والنخعي وميمون بن مهران من التوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waṣiyya variants conflict with the codex consonantal text and mass-transmitted reading, so they should be treated as tafsīr; qaḍā is the established reading.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يحمل ذلك التفسير لأنها قراءة مخالفة لسواد المصحف والمتواتر هو وقضى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They explain qaḍā here as meaning that God commanded.
rows.anchor: قضى هنا قال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة بمعنى أمر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأصحابه
rows.claim: They explain qaḍā as meaning that God enjoined or charged people with the command.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وأصحابه: بمعنى وصى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations gloss qaḍā as imposed, obligated, decreed, or perfected and firmly established.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أوجب وألزم وحكم. وقيل: بمعنى أحكم.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes the object of qaḍā to be God's command to worship Him alone, rather than worship itself.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وأقول إن المعنى وقضى ربك أمره ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's maneuver: the commentators take an taʿbudū as the object whether an is explicative or nominal, and qaḍā cannot mean a decree that does not occur.
rows.anchor: كأنه رام أن يترك قضى على مشهور موضوعها بمعنى قدر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows an taʿbudū to be an accusative complement meaning God obligated worship, with lā treated as extra.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: ويجوز أن تكون في موضع نصب أي ألزم ربك عبادته ولا زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parsing: illā governs the object of taʿbudū, requiring a negative or prohibitive construction, and the address is general to humankind.
rows.anchor: وهذا وهم لدخول إلا على مفعول تعبدوا فلزم أن يكون منفيا أو منهيا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also allows qaḍā in its ordinary sense, with the command addressed to believers among people until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يكون قضى على مشهورها في الكلام ويكون الضمير في تعبدوا للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches the preposition in bi-l-wālidayn to qaḍā, or supplies an omitted verb meaning that God enjoined kindness to parents.
rows.anchor: قال الحوفي: الباء متعلقة بقضى، ويجوز أن تكون متعلقة بفعل محذوف تقديره وأوصى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya coordinates kindness to parents with the preceding command not to worship other than God; alternatively it can begin a separate command.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: قوله وبالوالدين إحسانا عطف على أن الأولى أي أمر الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the preposition cannot attach to iḥsān because a verbal noun cannot have its complement placed before it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لا يجوز أن تتعلق الباء في بالوالدين بالإحسان لأن المصدر

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī instead treats the preposition as complement of iḥsān and allows it to precede, comparing the construction b-Zayd fa-murr.
rows.anchor: وقال الواحدي في البسيط: الباء في قوله بالوالدين من صلة الإحسان، وقدمت عليه كما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥsān can take either ilā or bi; when it means a verbal noun it cannot front its complement, but when it substitutes for the command aḥsinū, fronting is possible.
rows.anchor: وأحسن وأساء يتعدى بإلى وبالباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers an as an explicative particle, lā taʿbudū as prohibition, and iḥsānan as a verbal noun meaning a command coordinated with that prohibition.
rows.anchor: والذي نختاره أن تكون أن حرف تفسير ولا تعبدوا نهي وإحسانا مصدر بمعنى الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to honor parents is emphasized by being paired with exclusive worship, and by placing the parents before iḥsānan.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتنى بالأمر بالإحسان إلى الوالدين حيث قرن بقوله: لا تعبدوا وتقديمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true creator and provider; parents mediate a child's creation and labor for the child's welfare, which explains the pairing of their rights with worship.
rows.anchor: من حيث إنه تعالى هو الموجد حقيقة، والوالدان وساطة في إنشائه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls immā a conditional particle strengthened by mā, explaining the emphatic nūn on yablughanna.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إما هي الشرطية زيدت عليها ما توكيدا لها، ولذلك دخلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī's restriction conflicts with Sībawayh, who permits immā with emphasis, inna with emphasis, or immā without it.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره مخالف لمذهب سيبويه لأن مذهبه أنه يجوز أن يجمع بين إما ونون التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIndaka modifies yablughā; it means the parents are in the child's home and care, with no other caretaker because they are old, helpless, and dependent.
rows.anchor: وعندك ظرف معمول ليبلغن، ومعنى العندية هنا أنهما يكونان عنده في بيته وفي كنفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority reading, aḥaduhumā is the subject of yablughanna and aw kilāhumā is coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: وأحدهما فاعل يبلغن وأو كلاهما معطوف على أحدهما

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yablughanna with emphatic doubled nūn, with aḥaduhumā as its subject; Ibn Dhakwān is reported with light nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يبلغن بنون التوكيد الشديدة والفعل مسند إلى أحدهما

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: The two Kūfan readers, along with several named early readers, read the verb in the dual with a long alif and doubled emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان: إما يبلغان بألف التثنية ونون التوكيد المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed parse makes the alif a dual marker, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects it because a dual-marked verb requires a dual subject or a valid waw-coordinated pair.
rows.anchor: فقيل الألف علامة تثنية لا ضمير على لغة أكلوني البراغيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse makes the alif a pronoun for both parents, with aḥaduhumā as its substitute and kilāhumā coordinated with that substitute.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الألف ضمير الوالدين وأحدهما بدل من الضمير وكلاهما عطف على أحدهما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues kilāhumā is a substitute rather than emphasis: had emphasis been intended, the wording would have been only kilāhumā.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري. فإن قلت: لو قيل إما يبلغان كلاهما كان كلاهما توكيدا لا بدلا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls aḥaduhumā a distributive substitute for the dual pronoun and compares a poetic pair of legs, one sound and one crippled.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وعلى هذه القراءة الثالثة يعني يبلغان يكون قوله أحدهما بدلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains uff as an expression of aversion; the command requires gentle conduct and patience so parents are not even addressed with it in annoyance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أف كلمة كراهة بالغ تعالى في الوصية بالوالدين

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says uff is especially bad toward parents because it rejects gratitude, denies their upbringing, and defies God's command.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي: قال علماؤنا: وإنما صار قول أف للوالدين أردأ شيء

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī also explains uff as a transferred word for rejecting anything, citing Abraham's rejection of his people and their idols.
rows.anchor: وأف كلمة منقولة لكل شيء مرفوض ولذلك قال إبراهيم عليه السلام: أف لكم

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وعيسى ونافع وحفص
rows.claim: These readers pronounce uff with kasra, doubling, and tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وعيسى ونافع وحفص أف بالكسر والتشديد مع التنوين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر
rows.claim: These readers use the same kasra and doubling but omit tanwīn; other named readers have fatḥa, light, or differently inflected forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر كذلك بغير تنوين

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read uff with fatḥa and doubling, without tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر بفتحها مشددة من غير تنوين

rows.speaker: هارون
rows.claim: Hārūn reports a nominative form with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وحكى هارون قراءة بالرفع والتنوين

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads uff with ḍamma on the fāʾ and no tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال أف بضم الفاء من غير تنوين

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads the form in the accusative with doubled fāʾ and tanwīn; Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported with a light form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي أفا بالنصب والتشديد والتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's distributive-substitute analysis because that construction needs waw and kilāhumā denotes the same full dual referent.
rows.anchor: فليس من بدل التقسيم لأن شرط ذلك العطف بالواو، وأيضا فالبدل المقسم لا يصدق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī reportedly treats kilāhumā as emphasis by positing a deleted verb and an omitted emphasized pronoun, a deletion other grammarians reject.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن أبي علي أن كلاهما توكيد وهذا لا يتم إلا بأن يعرب أحدهما بدل بعض من كل

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl allow deletion of an emphasized expression while retaining its emphasis, with examples in nominative and accusative constructions.
rows.anchor: وقد أجازه سيبويه والخليل قال: مررت بزيد وإياي أخوه أنفسهما بالرفع والنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān's preferred parse makes aḥaduhumā a substitute for the pronoun and supplies a verb before kilāhumā, coordinating two clauses: one or both parents may reach old age.
rows.anchor: والذي نختاره أن يكون أحدهما بدلا من الضمير وكلاهما مرفوع بفعل محذوف تقديره أو يبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on saying uff entails a fortiori forbidding more severe insults or blows, though uff does not lexically denote every kind of injury.
rows.anchor: فالنهي عما هو أشد كالشتم والضرب هو بجهة الأولى، وليست دلالة أف على أنواع الإيذاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid applies the prohibition to seeing elderly parents' bowel or urine and not recoiling or saying uff; Abū Ḥayyān says the verse is broader.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إن معناه إذا رأيت منهما في حال الشيخ الغائط والبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition begins with even the mild expression of annoyance and then escalates to the stronger act of rebuking parents.
rows.anchor: ولما نهاه تعالى أن يقول لهما ما مدلوله أتضجر منكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because forbidding a mild expression already entails forbidding worse conduct a fortiori, the separate ban on rebuking parents bars scolding them for acts one dislikes.
rows.anchor: ارتقى إلى النهي عما هو من حيث الوضع أشد من أف وهو نهرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of saying uff or rebuking them, the child must use noble speech that combines kindness and excellent wording.
rows.anchor: وقل لهما بدل قول أف ونهرهما قولا كريما أي جامعا للمحاسن من البر وجودة اللفظ

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib describes noble speech as the wording a guilty servant uses when addressing a master.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المسيب: قول العبد المذنب للسيد اللفظ.

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar explains noble speech as addressing one's parents with affectionate titles such as father and mother.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر: أن تقول يا أبتاه يا أماه انتهى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling parents by their names is rude, though mentioning a parent's name indirectly is acceptable, as in ʿĀʾisha's statement that Abū Bakr gave her something.
rows.anchor: ولا تدعوهما بأسمائهما لأنه من الجفاء وسوء الأدب ولا بأس به في غير وجهه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says one should speak without raising one's gaze or staring fixedly at parents, since that conflicts with noble speech.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: تتكلم معهما بشرط أن لا ترفع إليهما بصرك ولا تشد إليهما نظرك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines noble speech as smooth, gentle wording without harshness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج قولا سهلا سلسا لا شراسة فيه

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl gives two images for lowering the wing: a bird shelters its young, and a bird lowers its wing when it stops flying or rising.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال في تقريره وجهان. أحدهما: أن الطائر إذا ضم فرخه إليه للتربية خفض له جناحه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes lowering the wing as a metaphor for making oneself humble and gentle toward one's parents; the word dhull emphasizes their exceptional right.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: استعارة أي اقطعهما جانب الذل منك ودمث لهما نفسك وخلقك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers two readings of wing of humility: a humble wing belonging to the person, or a low wing given figuratively to humility itself.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: ما معنى جناح الذل؟ قلت: فيه وجهان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second image personifies gentleness as humility, gives it a wing, then extends the metaphor by commanding that it be lowered.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه جعل اللين ذلا واستعار له جناحا ثم رشح هذا المجاز

rows.speaker: أبو تمام
rows.claim: An anecdote says Abū Tammām answered a request for literal water of blame by demanding a feather from the wing of humility.
rows.anchor: فقال له: حتى تأتيني بريشة من جناح الذل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's wings are the two sides; the phrase means lower one's side before parents and do not raise it in arrogance.
rows.anchor: وجناحا الإنسان جانباه، فالمعنى واخفض لهما جانبك ولا ترفعه فعل المتكبر عليهما.

rows.speaker: شاعر متأخر
rows.claim: A later poet illustrates the wing image by saying others feathered his wing with generosity, leaving him unable to fly away from them.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين فأحسن: أراشوا جناحي ثم بلوه بالندى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read al-dhull with ḍamma, while Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, al-Jaḥdarī, and Ibn Waththāb read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور من الذل بضم الذال. وقرأ ابن عباس وعروة بن جبير والجحدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra reading uses a metaphor from animal docility, while ḍamma denotes human abasement as the opposite of arrogance.
rows.anchor: وذلك على الاستعارة في الناس لأن ذلك يستعمل في الدواب في ضد الصعوبة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says min al-raḥma means because of compassion, or functions circumstantially with wing.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: من الرحمة أي من أجل الرحمة، أي من أجل رفقك بهما

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes min al-raḥma as specifying the kind or origin of the humility, which comes from compassion within the self.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: من الرحمة هنا لبيان الجنس أي إن هذا الخفض يكون من الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents' old-age dependence recalls the child's former dependence, deepening compassion; the prayer seeks God's lasting mercy, which human mercy cannot provide permanently.
rows.anchor: ثم نبه على العلة الموجبة للإحسان إليهما والبر بهما واسترحام الله لهما وهي تربيتهما له صغيرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the prayer for mercy was abrogated by the prohibition on seeking forgiveness for polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: نسخ الله من هذه الآية هذا اللفظ يعني وقل رب ارحمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views either restrict the prayer to polytheist parents or allow prayer for their guidance now and for mercy after they believe; Abū Ḥayyān favors no abrogation or restriction.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الكاف في كما للتعليل أي رب ارحمهما لتربيتهما لي

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses kamā as an accusative adjective of an omitted verbal noun: mercy like their raising the child when young.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: الكاف في موضع نصب نعت لمصدر محذوف تقديره رحمة مثل تربيتي صغيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding worship and parental kindness, God says He knows hidden intentions, since people may outwardly show devotion and respect without sincere inward purpose.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان ربما تظاهر بعبادة وإحسان إلى والديه دون عقد ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous people who lapse in worship or kindness but return to good are forgiven; the general meaning includes anyone who repents, even from wrongdoing against parents.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا عام لكل من فرطت منه جناية ثم تاب منها

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr applies the verse to a son confronting his father, while intending only good.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: هي في المبارزة تكون من الرجل إلى أبيه لا يريد بذلك إلا الخير.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the order to give the near kin their right was revealed concerning the Prophet's relatives.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: نزلت في قرابة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes the address as continuing the same general addressee and the right as kinship, relieving need, and assistance by every means.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه خطاب لمن خوطب بقوله إما يبلغن عندك الكبر

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn says the near kin are the Prophet's relatives, whose rights are paid from the public treasury.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن الحسين فيها: هم قرابة الرسول عليه السلام، أمر بإعطائهم حقوقهم من بيت المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse leaves the precise right and scope of near kin general, so Prophetic practice determines what is due and to whom.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الحق هنا مجمل وأن ذا القربى عام في ذي القرابة فيرجع في تعيين الحق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa requires support for poor, non-earning unmarriageable relatives when the giver is financially able.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة: أن القرابة إذا كانوا محارم فقراء عاجزين عن التكسب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires maintenance only for children and parents, as established in jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: وعند الشافعي: ينفق على الولد والوالدين فحسب على ما تقرر في كتب الفقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition addresses pre-Islamic wasteful spending, including sacrificing camels and gambling over them for pride and reputation; spending is barred outside good works and what draws one near God.
rows.anchor: وكانت الجاهلية تنحر إبلها وتتياسر عليها وتبذر أموالها في الفخر والسمعة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās define waste as spending wealth outside its proper right.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود وابن عباس: التبذير إنفاق المال في غير حق.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says spending all one's wealth for a proper purpose would not count as waste.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لو أنفق ماله كله في حق ما كان مبذرا.

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī defines waste as ruinous excess and infers that the ruler must interdict a spendthrift and limit spending to ordinary maintenance.
rows.anchor: وذكر الماوردي أنه الإسراف المتلف للمال، وقد احتج بهذه الآية على الحجر على المبذر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa does not permit legal interdiction solely for wasteful spending, even though it is prohibited.
rows.anchor: وأبو حنيفة لا يرى الحجر للتبذير وإن كان منهيا عنه

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ likewise treats kamā as a descriptor of an omitted verbal noun, meaning mercy like their mercy to the child.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: كما نعت لمصدر محذوف أي رحمة مثل رحمتهما

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī supports interdiction if wealth is spent on desires and likely to run out, but not when the principal is preserved.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي: يحجر عليه إن بذله في الشهوات وخيف عليه النفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling spendthrifts brothers of devils means their companionship in worldly life and in the Fire, and implies that their waste is disobedience or obedience to satanic prompting.
rows.anchor: وأخوة الشياطين كونهم قرناءهم في الدنيا وفي النار في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the phrase with the singular form akhwān al-shayṭān, as also found in Anas's codex.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك إخوان الشيطان على الإفراد وكذا ثبت في مصحف أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning Satan's disbelief warns people not to follow him, since he summons his party toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: وذكر كفر الشيطان لربه ليحذر ولا يطاع لأنه لا يدعو إلى خير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported occasion says people of Muzayna asked the Prophet for a mount; he had none, and they wept.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في ناس من مزينة استحملوا الرسول فقال:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report places the occasion among Bilāl, Ṣuhayb, Sālim, and Khabbāb, who asked for something the Prophet lacked and were turned away.
rows.anchor: وقيل في بلال وصهيب وسالم وخباب: سألوه ما لا يجد فأعرض عنهم.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says that when unable to give, the Prophet would say, May God provide for us and you from His bounty; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه عليه السلام كان بعد نزول هذه الآية إذا لم يكن عنده ما يعطي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿIkrima understand the hoped-for mercy as provision expected from God.
rows.anchor: فالرحمة على هذا الرزق المنتظر وهو قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes mercy as reward and says the verse concerns petitioners whom the Prophet refused because he knew they would misuse money; God ordered a kind response wishing them opening and reform.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الرحمة الأجر والثواب وإنما نزلت الآية في قوم كانوا يسألون رسول الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains turning away as embarrassment when one lacks what relatives or needy people ask for, and says the petitioner should still receive an answer.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وإن أعرضت عن ذي القربى والمسكين وابن السبيل حياء من الرد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports that the Prophet, when asked for something unavailable, would turn away and fall silent out of modesty.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سئل شيئا وليس عنده أعرض عن السائل وسكت حياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says turning away can mean inability to relieve need, not literally turning one's face; refusal is figuratively described as turning away.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى وإما تعرضن عنهم وإن لم تنفعهم وترفع خصاصتهم لعدم الاستطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes the pronoun to refer to needy kin and others; seeking God's mercy is a metonym for seeking provision, whose absence causes inability to give.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه تعالى لما أمر بإيتاء ذي القربى حقه ومن ذكر معه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes the hoped-for mercy a cause of the gentle answer and says compassion for them seeks God's mercy; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the syntax.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون ابتغاء رحمة من ربك علة لجواب الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase after the conditional answer's fa cannot govern an element before it, so al-Zamakhsharī's proposed attachment is grammatically invalid.
rows.anchor: وما أجازه لا يجوز لأن ما بعد فاء الجواب لا يعمل فيما قبله

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the pronoun refers to disbelievers who reject the Prophet, and mercy means victory over them or their guidance; the answer is verbal forbearance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: الضمير في عنهم عائد على المشركين

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī interprets the easy word as verbally managing or gently conciliating them.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول الميسور المداراة لهم باللسان قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives maysūr as something easy, comparing it with the paired verbs yasura and ʿasura; Abū Ḥayyān also records the transitive sense of preparing something for someone.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: يقال يسر الأمر وعسر مثل سعد ونحس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One occasion report says the verse came after the Prophet gave away his only shirt and was left naked.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في إعطائه صلى الله عليه وسلم قميصه ولم يكن له غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet gave one hundred camels each to al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna, then raised al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's fifty to one hundred before the verse came.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعطى الأقرع بن حابس مائة من الإبل، وعيينة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses concrete images for abstract conduct: miserliness is a hand bound to the neck, preventing it from moving to give.
rows.anchor: وهذه استعارة استعير فيها المحسوس للمعقول، وذلك أن البخل معنى قائم بالإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand represents giving and receiving; spreading it represents spending money away, while closing it retains what is held.
rows.anchor: وذكر اليد لأن بها الأخذ والإعطاء، واستعير بسط اليد لإذهاب المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired images balance one another: a bound hand is a forceful closing and an open hand disperses its contents; Abū Tammām also used this contrast.
rows.anchor: وطابق في الاستعارة بين بسط اليد وقبضها من حيث المعنى لأن جعل اليد مغلولة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the verse as a representation of the miser and the squanderer and a command to the middle course between extravagance and stinginess.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هذا تمثيل لمنع الشحيح وإعطاء المسرف، أمر بالاقتصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent addressee is the Prophet's community: the Prophet kept nothing for the next day, and Abū Bakr could give all his wealth through complete trust in God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه مراد بالخطاب أمة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وإلا فهو صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and others explain the command as not withholding required charity and not spending on what God has forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وغيره: المعنى لا تمسك عن النفقة فيما أمرتك به من الحق

rows.speaker: قالون
rows.claim: Qālūn is reported to read al-basṭ with ṣād.
rows.anchor: وروي عن قالون: كل البصط بالصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blame corresponds to miserliness and exhaustion to spending everything; the two outcomes describe the two extremes of the conditional warning.
rows.anchor: فالملوم راجع لقوله: ولا تجعل يدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse consoles the Prophet: limited means do not signal God's contempt or stinginess, since provision expands or contracts by divine will and wisdom for servants' benefit.
rows.anchor: بأن ذلك ليس بهوان منك عليه ولا لبخل به عليك، ولكن لأن بسط الرزق

rows.speaker: شاعر القصيدة اليتيمة
rows.claim: A line in the so-called Orphan Poem counsels making a petitioner feel at ease and, if unable to give, answering kindly.
rows.anchor: إن لم يكن فليحسن الرد

rows.speaker: شاعر آخر
rows.claim: Another poet says that even without money to give, he remains gentle and seekers receive either a gift or a gracious refusal.
rows.anchor: إن لم يكن ورق يوما أجود به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God has just been described as controlling provision, the text forbids killing children from fear of poverty and assures provision for them and their parents.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى أنه هو المتكفل بأرزاق العباد حيث قال إن ربك يبسط الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between fearing poverty and already being poor, and between the order of the two recipients of provision, was explained under a parallel verse in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير نظير هذه الآية، والفرق بين خشية إملاق ومن إملاق

rows.speaker: الأعمش وابن وثاب
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb read the prohibition with a doubled verb form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن وثاب: ولا تقتلوا بالتضعيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads khashyatan with kasra on its first letter.
rows.anchor: وقرىء خشية بكسر الخاء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read khaṭʾan with kasra on khāʾ and a quiescent ṭāʾ; Ibn Kathīr and many others use a lengthened form with open ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور خطأ بكسر الخاء وسكون الطاء

rows.speaker: النحاس وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says he cannot parse the lengthened reading, and Abū Ḥātim calls it an error.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: لا أعرف لهذه القراءة وجها ولذلك جعلها أبو حاتم غلطا.

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Fārisī derives the lengthened form as a verbal noun from khāṭaʾa, although the direct verb is unattested; forms of takhāṭaʾa show the root, and the killers miss justice and right.
rows.anchor: وقال الفارسي: هي مصدر من خاطأ يخاطىء وإن كنا لم نجد خاطأ

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Ibn Dhakwān reads khaṭaʾ in the pattern of nabaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن ذكوان خطأ على وزن نبأ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan has a lengthened form with both initial and ṭāʾ open, analyzed by Ibn Jinnī as a noun of the verb akhṭaʾa; Abū Ḥātim rejects it as unknown.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن خطاء بفتحهما والمد جعله اسم مصدر من أخطأ كالعطاء

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء والزهري
rows.claim: Other transmitted forms drop the hamza into a long vowel; the readings are related to خطئ, moral error, and أخطأ, error of judgment, which can substitute for one another.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا خطى كهوى خفف الهمزة فانقلبت ألفا

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads khaṭaʾ with fatḥa on the initial letter, a short hamza, and ṭāʾ still, as a third verbal noun from khaṭiʾa.
rows.anchor: وجاء عن ابن عامر خطأ بالفتح والقصر مع إسكان الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding killing children, the text forbids the illicit act that can produce them; forbidding approaching zinā entails forbidding zinā itself.
rows.anchor: لما نهى تعالى عن قتل الأولاد نهى عن التسبب في إيجاده من الطريق غير المشروعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word zinā is usually shortened, but lengthening is also a lexical form, not merely poetic license.
rows.anchor: والزنا الأكثر فيه القصر ويمد لغة لا ضرورة

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line uses the lengthened form of zinā and links it to knowledge of the penalty for fornication.
rows.anchor: ومن المد قول الشاعر وهو الفرزدق:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zinā is an exceptionally ugly sin, and its path is evil because it leads to the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي معصية فاحشة أي قبيحة زائدة في القبح وساء سبيلا أي وبئس طريقا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya parses sabīlan as a specification, with the implied sense that its path is bad.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وسبيلا نصب على التمييز التقدير، وساء سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says that if sabīlan is a specification, it explains the hidden subject of sāʾa and leaves the condemned object omitted; it cannot parse as sāʾa sabīlahu sabīlan.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان سبيلا نصبا على التمييز فإنما هو تمييز للمضمر المستكن في ساء

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the prohibition on killing a protected person was the first Qur'anic revelation concerning murder.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: هذه أول ما نزل من القرآن في شأن القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves from child-killing and the illicit means of conception to killing people generally; each prohibition stands independently rather than depending syntactically on qaḍā.
rows.anchor: ولما نهى عن قتل الأولاد وعن إيجادهم من الطريق غير المشروعة نهى عن قتل النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maẓlūman is a circumstantial accusative for the implicit subject of qutila, meaning the person was killed wrongfully.
rows.anchor: وانتصب مظلوما على الحال من الضمير المستكن في قتل والمعنى أنه قتل بغير حق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his school include male, female, and minor heirs as the victim's walī, with shares proportionate to inheritance.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه اندراج من يرث من الرجال والنساء والصبيان في الولي

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik excludes women from retaliation rights and assigns qisas to men.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: ليس للنساء شيء من القصاص، وإنما القصاص للرجال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the walī's authority as control to retaliate or as evidence proving the claim against the killer.
rows.anchor: وللسلطان التسلط على القاتل في الاقتصاص منه أو حجة يثبت بها عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take authority to mean proof or the right to choose retaliation or pardon.
rows.anchor: والسلطان الحجة والملك الذي جعل إليه من التخيير في قبول الدم أو العفو

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda defines the authority granted to the victim's heir as retaliation itself.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: السلطان القود

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan likewise explains the authority as the right of retaliation.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن القود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid takes the authority to mean proof or argument.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد الحجة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd understands it as the ruler who ensures the heir receives justice.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الوالي أي واليا ينصفه في حقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan say excess means killing someone other than the actual killer.
rows.anchor: أن يقتل غير القاتل قاله ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says excess is killing two people for one victim.
rows.anchor: أو يقتل اثنين بواحد قاله ابن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says excess includes killing someone more distinguished than the person killed.
rows.anchor: أو أشرف من الذي قتل قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says excess includes mutilating the killer.
rows.anchor: أو يمثل قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says excess includes taking vengeance personally instead of going through the ruler.
rows.anchor: أو يتولى القاتل دون السلطان ذكره الزجاج

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the general authority is explained by the law of retaliation, which lets the heir choose qisas or blood money; he cites a Prophetic report at the Conquest granting those alternatives.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: السلطنة مجملة يفسرها كتب عليكم القصاص الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Rāzī's reading that the verse urges acceptance of blood money or pardon: a rightful killing of the actual murderer is not itself excess.
rows.anchor: ولو سلم أن في بمعنى الباء لم يكن صحيح المعنى، لأن من قتل بحق قاتل موليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent prohibition targets pre-Islamic excess: killing groups for one victim, killing nonkillers, mutilation, and reciprocal vengeance.
rows.anchor: وإنما الظاهر والله أعلم النهي عما كانت الجاهلية تفعله من قتل الجماعة بالواحد

rows.speaker: مهلهل
rows.claim: Mihlal's verse threatens retaliation for the killing of Jubayr ibn al-Ḥārith, illustrating reciprocal vengeance beyond the actual killer.
rows.anchor: وقال مهلهل حين قتل بجير بن الحارث بن عباد: بؤ بشسع نعل كليب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the claim that the pronoun in fa-lā yusrif refers back to the killer rather than the victim's heir.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن الضمير في فلا يسرف ليس عائدا على الولي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read fa-lā yusrif with third-person ya; several readers instead use second-person tā, apparently addressing the heir.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فلا يسرف بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the second-person reading addresses the Prophet and later rulers, commanding them not to kill anyone besides the killer.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والأئمة من بعده

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم السراج
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Abū Muslim al-Sarrāj has the indicative yusrifu, used with prohibitive force; Abū Ḥayyān cautions against using him as a reading authority.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية في الاحتجاج بأبي مسلم في القراءة نظر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's manuscript reports a reading, fa-lā tusrifū fī al-qatl inna walī al-maqtūl kāna manṣūran; Abū Ḥayyān treats the latter phrase as explanation, not a canonical reading.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي فلا تسرفوا في القتل إن ولي المقتول كان منصورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the standard wording, innahu most naturally refers to the heir, supported by the legally granted qisas and by the ruler or believers helping secure his right.
rows.anchor: والضمير في إنه عائد على الولي لتناسق الضمائر ونصره إياه بأن أوجب له القصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding harm to lives, the text forbids taking property; orphans are singled out because their youth leaves them too weak to defend their wealth.
rows.anchor: لما نهى عن إتلاف النفوس نهى عن أخذ الأموال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report declares people's blood, property, and honor inviolable.
rows.anchor: فإن دماءكم وأموالكم وأعراضكم حرام عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that the orphan-property verse was also explained near the end of al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير هذه الآية في أواخر الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to fulfill covenants broadly covers obligations between a person and God, and agreements with another person made in obedience.
rows.anchor: وأوفوا بالعهد عام فيما عقده الإنساب بينه وبين ربه، أو بينه وبين ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that a covenant will be questioned may personify the covenant to dramatize its keeping or breach and the consequences of breaking it.
rows.anchor: ظاهره أن العهد هو المسئول من المعاهد أن يفي به ولا يضيعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted noun: the person bound by the covenant will be asked about it if he fails to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو على حذف مضاف أي إن ذا العهد كان مسؤولا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fulfill the measure is directed to sellers, since buyers are not described as measuring out goods.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله وأوفوا الكيل دلالة على أن الكيل هو على البائع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the qistās as a balance or scale, also called al-qubbān or al-qalastūn.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: بالقسطاس القبان وهو القلسطون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets qistās as justice rather than as an instrument.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالقسطاس العدل لا أنه آلة.

rows.speaker: الأخوان وحفص
rows.claim: The two Kūfan readers and Ḥafṣ pronounce qistās with kasra on qāf; the other canonical readers use ḍamma, and another group replaces the first sīn with ṣād.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وحفص بكسر القاف، وباقي السبعة بضمها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya derives the word from qasṭ, taking its form as an emphatic expression of fairness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: واللفظية للمبالغة من القسط انتهى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects derivation from qasṭ because the roots differ unless the final sīn is treated as an unusual augment.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون من القسط لاختلاف المادتين لأن القسط مادته ق س ط

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers innahu to refer to the murdered victim, since he is wronged and scriptural usage associates support with the wronged.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهو أرجح لأنه المظلوم، ولفظة النصر تقارن الظلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says the pronoun refers to the killer: being killed in this world saves him from punishment in the next; Abū Ḥayyān calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: على القاتل لأنه إذا قتل في الدنيا وخلص بذلك من عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the pronoun refers to a killer whom the heir kills unjustly, since the excessive avenger is then subject to retaliation; Abū Ḥayyān calls this very remote.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وإنما يعني أن يكون الضمير في أنه الذي بقتله الولي بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Full measure and just weighing are better because fairness satisfies people and delivers their due; the outcome is best because no worldly or otherworldly liability remains.
rows.anchor: ذلك خير أي الإيفاء والوزن لأن فيه تطييب النفوس بالاتسام بالعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fair dealing also builds a reputation for avoiding short measure, making others trust the merchant and incline toward him.
rows.anchor: وإنما كانت عاقبته أحسن لأنه اشتهر بالاحتراز عن التطفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage follows three commands—keeping covenants, full measure, fair weighing—with three prohibitions: following without knowledge, arrogant walking, and associating another god.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك بثلاثة أمناه: ولا تقف ولا تمش ولا تجعل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not follow anything unknown, whether in speech or action; this includes making claims without knowledge and following an unverified report.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ولا تقف لا تتبع ما لا علم لك به من قول أو فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the rule also encompasses rejection of taqlīd, since it follows something without knowing its correctness.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه النهي عن اتباع التقليد لأنه اتباع بما لا يعلم صحته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command as forbidding an accusation for which one has no knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معناه لا ترم أحدا بما لا تعلم.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says not to claim one saw, heard, or knew something when one did not.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة لا تقل رأيت ولم تره وسمعت ولم تسمعه وعلمت ولم تعلمه

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya applies the verse to false testimony.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنيفة: لا تشهد بالزور

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verb is used specifically for slander and insult.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ولا تقل لكنها كلمة تستعمل في القذف والعضه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report threatens imprisonment in the sludge of corruption for falsely accusing a believer until the accuser produces a defense; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قفا مؤمنا بما ليس فيه حبسه الله في ردغة الخبال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying identifies his lineage as descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kināna and forbids accusing them or denying their father.
rows.anchor: نحن بنو النضر بن كنانة لا تقفو منا ولا ننتفي من أبينا

rows.speaker: النابغة الجعدي
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī's verse illustrates women who do not follow gossip or slander.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول النابغة الجعدي:
ومثل الدمى شم العرانين ساكن

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt's line says he will not accuse an innocent person without cause or pursue slander against nursing women.
rows.anchor:
وقال الكميت
فلا أرمي البريء بغير ذنب ... ولا أقفو الحواضن إن قفينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase when you measure emphasizes giving full measure at the time of measuring, without postponing a shortfall and making it good later.
rows.anchor: إذا كلتم أي وقت كيلكم على سبيل التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general rule is not to follow what is unknown; the named interpretations are particular applications of that universal rule.
rows.anchor: وحاصل هذا أنه نهى عن اتباع ما لا يكون معلوما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says opponents of legal reasoning misuse this verse, because ijtihād is a form of knowledge and law treats predominant probability as knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وقد استدل به مبطل الاجتهاد ولم يصح لأن ذلك نوع من العلم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read wa-lā taqfu with the weak wāw omitted in the jussive; Zayd ibn ʿAlī retains it, attested dialectally or as poetic license.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ولا تقف بحذف الواو للجزم مضارع قفا.

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads wa-lā taqfū with the wāw retained, as in poetry that retains a weak ending after a jussive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ولا تقفو بإثبات الواو

rows.speaker: معاذ القارئ
rows.claim: Muʿādh al-Qāriʾ reads the verb like taqil, from qāfa yaqūfu; the forms qāfa and qafā coexist and are not a metathesis of one another.
rows.anchor: وقرأ معاذ القارئ: ولا تقف مثل تقل، من قاف يقوف

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ proposes that qāfa is inverted from qafā, a derivation Abū Ḥayyān rejects.
rows.anchor: وليس قاف مقلوبا من قفا كما جوزه صاحب اللوامح

rows.speaker: الجراح العقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Jarrāḥ al-ʿUqaylī reads al-fuʾād with open fāʾ and wāw, from changing hamza to wāw after ḍamma; Abū Ḥātim and others reject the dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجراح العقيلي: والفؤاد بفتح الفاء والواو قلبت الهمزة واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause's prepositional phrase cannot attach to ʿilm if its governed complement precedes the governing word.
rows.anchor: وبه لا تتعلق بعلم لأنه يتقدم معموله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning hearing, sight, and heart indicates that knowledge comes from sensory faculties and reason, in Qur'anic order from hearing to sight to heart.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد دليل على أن العلوم مستفادة من الحواس

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the rational demonstrative أولئك fits because the faculties perceive and are treated as accountable.
rows.anchor: وتخيل ابن عطية أنه يختص بالعاقل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh explains the rational pronoun in the verse about Joseph's dream by the stars' being described as prostrating, an act of rational beings.
rows.anchor: وقد قال سيبويه رحمه الله في قوله تعالى: رأيتهم لي ساجدين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Arabic uses أولئك for both rational beings and things, citing a line transmitted with the days after al-Liwāʾ.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزجاج أن العرب تعبر عمن يعقل وعما لا يعقل بأولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the report's authority warrants caution and notes that some transmit the poem as al-aqwām rather than al-ayyām; grammarians nevertheless cite the latter, and the demonstrative can refer to non-rational things.
rows.anchor: وأما حكاية أبي إسحاق عن اللغة فأمر يوقف عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull is the subject, its clause is the predicate, and the pronouns in kāna and masʾūlan return to kull.
rows.anchor: وكل مبتدأ والجملة خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ʿanhu most naturally refers to what one lacks knowledge of: each faculty is answerable for the absence of knowledge about it.
rows.anchor: والضمير في عنه عائد على ما من قوله ما ليس لك به علم فيكون المعنى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the faculties will testify, as in the verse where tongues, hands, and feet bear witness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يستشهد بها كما قال يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī assigns the heart what it believed, hearing what it heard, and sight what it saw.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي في أحكامه: يسأل الفؤاد عما اعتقده، والسمع عما سمع

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the person's senses are questioned about ignorant claims, then refute him, producing extreme disgrace.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: إن الله تعالى يسأل سمع الإنسان وبصره وفؤاده عما قال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses ʿanhu as a fronted passive subject and explains that each faculty is questioned about its use; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the word order and also restores ilā with naẓara.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وعنه في موضع الرفع بالفاعلية، أي كل واحد منها كان مسؤولا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maraḥan is a circumstantial accusative meaning exuberantly, possibly with an omitted noun meaning one possessed of exuberance; taking it as purpose is unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وانتصب مرحا على الحال أي مرحا كما تقول: جاء زيد ركضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exuberance means joy and contentment with comfort, which commonly brings pride and conceit; the next clause explains why such pride is misplaced.
rows.anchor: وتقدم أن المرح هو السرور والاغتباط بالراحة والفرح وكأنه ضمن معنى الاختيال

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group, as transmitted by Yaʿqūb, reads maraḥan with kasra on rāʾ to mean walking proudly and conceitedly.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة فيما حكى يعقوب: مرحا بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets tearing earth as walking on one's heels in pride and reaching mountains as walking on one's toes in boastful extension; human ability falls far short of either.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لن تخرق بمشيك على عقبيك كبرا وتنعما، ولن تبلغ الجبال بالمشي على صدور قدميك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj paraphrases the verse as forbidding a conceited, boastful walk, like other Qur'anic commands to walk humbly and deliberately.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: لا تمش في الأرض مختالا فخورا، ونظيره:

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the images literally—one cannot punch a hole in earth or reach mountains by stretching—and sees them as sarcasm against the arrogant.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لن تخرق الأرض لن تجعل فيها خرقا بدوسك لها

rows.speaker: الجراح الأعرابي
rows.claim: Al-Jarrāḥ al-Aʿrābī reads takhriq with ḍamma on rāʾ; Abū Ḥātim says the dialect is unknown.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجراح الأعرابي: لن تخرق بضم الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says people are confined between two inanimate limits they cannot pierce or reach, which makes arrogance inappropriate; a verse urges walking humbly over the earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أشير بذلك إلى أن الإنسان محصور بين جمادين ضعيف عن التأثير فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān considers ṭūlan best parsed as specification of the amount of one's height; alternative grammarians offer circumstantial, purpose, or cognate-accusative parses.
rows.anchor: والأجود انتصاب قوله طولا على التمييز، أي لن يبلغ طولك الجبال

rows.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر والأعرج
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the word as feminine accusative sayyiʾatan; other canonical readers use masculine sayyiʾuhu, and several other forms are transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر والأعرج سيئة بالنصب والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine reading points to the last two prohibitions, or possibly to all the prohibitions earlier in the sūra.
rows.anchor: فأما القراءة الأولى فالظاهر أن ذلك إشارة إلى مصدري النهيين السابقين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says siʾah functions as a noun like dhanb rather than as an adjective, so grammatical gender need not match its referent; Abū Ḥayyān calls the analysis sound.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: السيئة في حكم الأسماء بمنزلة الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians variously parse makrūhan as a second predicate of kāna, a weak derived substitute, or a circumstantial description attached to the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا في مكروها أن يكون خبرا ثانيا لكان على مذهب من يجيز تعداد الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making masculine makrūhan an adjective of feminine sayyiʾah is weak when the adjective follows and refers back by pronoun, though the reverse order can be idiomatic.
rows.anchor: وضعف هذا بأن جواز ذلك إنما هو في الإسناد إلى المؤنث المجازي إذا تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With masculine possessive sayyiʾuhu, sayyiʾah is the name of kāna and makrūhan its predicate; the singular bad thing represents the prohibited part among prior good and bad duties.
rows.anchor: وأما من قرأ سيئه بالتذكير والإضافة فسيئة اسم كان ومكروها الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural reading from ʿAbd Allāh uses a rare singular masculine predicate to report a plural, compared with a poetic line.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة عبد الله فتخرج على أن يكون مما أخبر فيه عن الجمع إخبار الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative covers twenty-four kinds of duties from the prohibition on associating another god through the prohibition on arrogant walking.
rows.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى جميع أنواع التكاليف من قوله لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These commands and prohibitions are part of what was revealed, since further teachings were revealed too; their wisdom lies in monotheism, obedience, turning from this world, and seeking the next.
rows.anchor: إلى الأمر بالتوحيد وأنواع الطاعات والإعراض عن الدنيا والإقبال على الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The directives accord with reason and are laws shared by religions that cannot be abrogated.
rows.anchor: والعقول تدل على صحتها وهي شرائع في جميع الأديان لا تقبل النسخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these directives were on Moses's tablets, linking them to the revelation of admonition and detailed instruction on the tablets.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن هذه الآيات كانت في ألواح موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on associating partners frames the list; the first ending promises disgrace and abandonment, while the second warns of blame and banishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: وكرر تعالى النهي عن الشرك، ففي النهي الأول. فتقعد مذموما مخذولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being disgraced means one's deed is called shameful, while being blamed means being asked afterward why one acted and gained only harm; abandonment is lack of help, banishment is humiliating expulsion.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين مذموم وملوم أن كونه مذموما أن يذكر أن الفعل الذي أقدم عليه قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disgrace and abandonment characterize worldly life, while blame and expulsion characterize the Hereafter; the prohibitions address any listener, not specifically the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وكان وصف الذم والخذلان يكون في الدنيا ووصف اللوم والدحور يكون في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says monotheism frames the list because it is the root and key of wisdom; without it even profound wisdom and learning do not benefit their holders.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ولقد جعل الله عز وعلا فاتحتها وخاتمتها النهي عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting claims of a divine partner, the passage refutes claims of divine offspring; its question rebukes those who call angels God's daughters and asks whether God favored them with sons while taking females for Himself.
rows.anchor: لما نبه تعالى على فساد من أثبت لله شريكا ونظيرا أتبعه بفساد طريقة من أثبت لله ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address targets people who regarded angels as God's daughters; aṣfākum means chose or favored you, as in the parallel contrast of daughters for God and sons for them.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لمن اعتقد أن الملائكة بنات الله ومعنى أفأصفاكم آثركم وخصكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim reverses their own social reasoning: people reserve the best things for themselves, yet assign to God what they dislike and femininity to the noblest created beings.
rows.anchor: وهذا خلاف الحكمة وما عليه معقولكم وعادتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution is especially monstrous because they ascribe offspring to God, privilege themselves over Him, assign Him what they hate, and call the angels feminine.
rows.anchor: ومعنى عظيما مبالغا في المنكر والقبح حيث أضفتم إليه الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarrafnā literally means turning something from one direction to another and became a metaphor for explaining it through varied presentations.
rows.anchor: والتصريف لغة صرف الشيء من جهة إلى جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's doubled form is explained as presenting varied material—promise and warning, clear and ambiguous, command and prohibition, abrogating and abrogated, reports, and parables—with the object omitted.
rows.anchor: ولقد صرفنا بتشديد الراء. فقال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the Qur'an came down in installments, meaning Gabriel was sent repeatedly; the object is omitted as Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لم ننزله مرة واحدة بل نجوما ومعناه أكثرنا صرف جبريل إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that fī is extra in hādhā al-Qurʾāni is weak because fī is not used redundantly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في زائدة أي صرفنا هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī restricts the reference to repeated arguments against the claim that God has daughters, taking the object as the discourse or an omitted pronoun for that subject; other interpreters take a broader range of topics.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يجوز أن يريد بهذا القرآن إبطال إضافتهم إلى الله البنات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ṣarrafnā with a light rāʾ; al-Lawāmiʿ treats it as synonymous with the majority form, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya says it turns people toward guidance through the call to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بتخفيف الراء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read li-yadhdhakkarū, with tāʾ assimilated into dhāl, meaning that people may remember and take heed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ليذكروا أي ليتذكروا من التذكير، أدغمت التاء في الذال

rows.speaker: الأخوان وطلحة وابن وثاب والأعمش
rows.claim: These readers use a form from dhikr, meaning that people may be admonished, reflect on the proofs, and become reassured by them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وطلحة وابن وثاب والأعمش ليذكروا بسكون الذال وضم الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the varied presentation, the disbelievers only flee farther from truth, as in verses where reminders increase defilement or drive people away like fleeing asses.
rows.anchor: وما يزيدهم أي التصريف إلا نفورا أي بعدا وفرارا عن الحق

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read the phrase as yaqūlūn with yāʾ; most readers use tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحفص كما يقولون بالياء من تحت، والجمهور بالتاء

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وأبو علي الفارسي والنقاش والمتكلمون
rows.claim: They explain the hypothetical rival gods as seeking to overpower the Lord of the Throne and disrupt His kingdom, like rival kings; this expresses the argument from mutual prevention.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا إلى مغالبته وإفساد ملكه
